title: Lake Brennersee Gries am Brenner
name: Lake Brennersee Gries am Brenner
kurzbeschreibung: Brennersee at 1,310 m near the mountain pass: a pristine mountain lake and source of the Sill with emerald-green waters, a circular lakeside trail, and rich fish stocks.
beschreibung:
Overview

The idyllic Brennersee is situated in the upper Wipptal in the municipality of Gries am Brenner (Bezirk Innsbruck-Land) at an elevation of 1,310 metres above sea level, just about one kilometre north of the European mountain pass at Brennerpass on the border with Südtirol. Fed by the crystal-clear mountain streams of the surrounding Tuxer and Stubaier Alpen, the natural lake covers approximately 5.5 hectares and is the source of Tyrol's major river, the Sill, which flows from here through the entire Wipptal to Innsbruck. Despite its proximity to the historic transit route, the lake surprises visitors with its densely wooded, peaceful setting and crystalline alpine waters.

Natural Idyll, Lakeside Trail & Fishing Paradise

Surrounded by dense spruce and larch forests and rugged mountain slopes, the up to twelve-metre-deep lake shimmers in vibrant emerald and turquoise tones. A flat, gravelled circular lakeside trail leads completely around the lake in about 45 minutes of leisurely walking. Along the path, rustic wooden benches and shaded sunbathing lawns invite visitors to linger and observe nature. Due to its cool water temperatures (rarely exceeding 14 °C even in midsummer), the lake is only occasionally used by hardy swimmers; however, it is renowned among anglers as a premier spot for brown trout, rainbow trout, and char. In winter, the lake reliably freezes over, transforming into an enchanting icy wonderland for winter hikers.

Visit & Getting There

Brennersee is freely accessible year-round and free of charge. Getting there by car: Via the Brenner federal road B182 from Innsbruck via Matrei and Steinach towards Brennerpass; shortly before the border, a small road branches off to the left towards the lake (free parking is available directly on the lake shore). By public transport: ÖBB/S-Bahn (line S3) to Brennersee or Brenner station, from where a short walk takes around ten minutes directly to the lake.

Tips

The circular lakeside path is flat and easily accessible for prams and wheelchairs. Combine your visit with a trip to the nearby Brennerpass or explore the wildly romantic Vennatal, which extends directly east of the lake into the Tuxer Alpen and is recognised as a botanical protected area of European significance.
